name: Tsurumaru (2011 livery)
description: All white. The red Tsurumaru (a crane with its wings raised in a circle, 'JAL' in white at its foot) big on a plain white fin, and 'JAPAN AIRLINES' in heavy, wide, slanted black capitals over the forward windows. White engines; on the A350s the sharklets fade to red at the tip.

sources.note: The Tsurumaru returned to the fleet from April 2011, replacing the 2002 'Arc of the Sun'.

logos.description: The Tsurumaru: a red disc formed by a crane's two raised, feathered wings curving up round it, its long neck in an S and head with a pointed beak at the top facing left, the white of the fin showing through as the crane's body; 'JAL' in white italic capitals across the bottom of the disc. The same artwork on both sides (the crane faces aft on the right).
A small Japanese flag (Hinomaru) just aft of the titles, at the same place on both sides (measured on the right, where it sits just aft of the 'J').

titles.style: Heavy, wide, italic capitals with squared counters, close-set, over the windows from about the first door to ahead of the wing.

notes: Measured on an A350-1000 from the right (mirrored to the left: the titles span the same stretch of fuselage on both sides). The A350-900s (JA01XJ-JA16XJ) add large red 'AIRBUS A350' titles on the rear fuselage ('AIRBUS' small, 'A350' big in outline-striped figures); the A350-1000s don't. Not drawn: the registration, the type, a small UNICEF 'we support' mark aft. Belly white, as the lower sides show; not seen squarely. 737-800 winglets not checked. The 2002-2011 'Arc of the Sun' scheme (a red-to-gold sweep on the fin) has been gone from the fleet since repainting finished in the mid-2010s. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on the 737-800 (the commonest type, JA338J and JA340J): the title runs from just aft of the first door to the overwing exits (0.184, run 0.304), its baseline a little above the window tops; on the A350 it is relatively shorter (0.132, run 0.254).
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation. The Tsurumaru scheme came back in April 2011 after JAL's restructuring, replacing the 2002 'Arc of the Sun'; it's the 1959-2002 crane, redrawn, without the old cheatlines.
